title: Quiz: Big Data Applications in SQC — EWMA, CUSUM, and ML Integration

questions.text: An EWMA chart uses λ = 0.2 and starts at z₀ = μ₀ = 50. The first observation is x₁ = 54. What is z₁?
questions.explanation: z₁ = λ × x₁ + (1 − λ) × z₀ = 0.2 × 54 + 0.8 × 50 = 10.8 + 40.0 = 50.8. The EWMA statistic gives only 20% weight to the new observation and 80% to the previous value, smoothing out the effect of the single outlier.

questions.text: In a tabular CUSUM chart with K = 0.5σ and H = 5σ, a process shift of +1σ is introduced. The CUSUM statistic C⁺ starts at 0. After the first out-of-control observation x₁ = μ₀ + 1.2σ, what is C₁⁺?
questions.explanation: C₁⁺ = max(0, x₁ − (μ₀ + K) + C₀⁺) = max(0, (μ₀ + 1.2σ) − (μ₀ + 0.5σ) + 0) = max(0, 0.7σ) = 0.7σ. The CUSUM accumulates the excess above the allowance K at each step.

questions.text: Which statement correctly explains why the EWMA chart detects small sustained process shifts faster than the Shewhart Xbar chart?
options: EWMA accumulates information from all past observations, so small consistent shifts build up in the statistic over time
EWMA uses wider control limits, making it easier for any observation to cross the boundary
EWMA ignores recent observations, focusing only on long-run history
EWMA uses a non-parametric test that does not require normality
questions.explanation: The Shewhart chart uses only the most recent point. EWMA accumulates a weighted average of all past observations. A small sustained shift of +0.5σ contributes +0.5σ × λ to z_t at each step; after many steps the EWMA statistic drifts clearly beyond the control limits, even though no single observation was far enough to signal on the Shewhart chart.

questions.text: In a Big Data SPC pipeline, which ML technique is most appropriate for detecting that a process has moved out of control when the fault pattern is unknown and no labelled historical examples of out-of-control conditions exist?
options: k-means clustering on the last 10 observations
questions.explanation: When no labelled fault examples exist, supervised classification cannot be trained. Isolation Forest is an unsupervised anomaly detection algorithm that isolates anomalous observations by randomly partitioning the feature space — points that are isolated with fewer splits are flagged as anomalies, without needing prior knowledge of what faults look like.

questions.text: A smaller EWMA smoothing parameter λ (e.g. 0.05) makes the chart more sensitive to large sudden jumps but slower to detect small sustained drifts.
questions.explanation: The relationship is reversed. A small λ gives heavy weight to historical values, producing a heavily smoothed statistic that changes slowly — it detects small sustained shifts well but responds slowly to sudden large jumps. A large λ (e.g. 0.4–0.5) responds quickly to sudden jumps but provides less smoothing, making it similar to the Shewhart chart and less sensitive to gradual drift.
